post_topic: LLM-agnostic architecture vs. vendor lock-in: why enterprises are buying the wrong thing
scene_description: A diagram showing a provider-agnostic orchestration layer — a single routing table — sitting between a calling application and three labeled endpoints: Azure OpenAI, Bedrock, and a local Ollama instance. On one side, a tightly coupled SDK path is marked with warning indicators representing token limit changes, schema shifts, and region-inconsistent rate limiting; on the other side, the abstracted interface shows a unified governance layer handling audit logging and HITL escalation triggers cleanly across all three providers. The contrast highlights the fragility of single-vendor lock-in versus the stability of a config-driven, LLM-agnostic foundation built for Cloud Decoded.
